dossier.public_summary: The 14.6-day dip changes depth by a factor of 10 between TESS sectors and between individual transits (including a null transit), which a planet must not do. A second strong dip about a third as deep as the main one and the star’s large spot variability indicate the signal is stellar variability or a small-star eclipse on the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor >10 between sectors within the same SPOC 2-min source (p_constant 5.517e-17). A planet on the target must have a constant depth; this aperture-independent variation points to a false signal, spots/folded variability or a blended eclipse.

reasons.why: Individual dips are inconsistent with a constant depth; with only 5 transits the top 3 carry 0.994 of the signal and two strong outliers near 1000 ppm drive the detection while sector 27 shows a null dip. True planets show repeatable depths.

reasons.why: A significant secondary dip at 38% of transit depth (snr 5.518 well above best brightening snr 4.092) is inconsistent with a planet and favours a stellar eclipsing binary on the target / diluted binary.

Target is a strong variable (teff 4875 K) with spot phases matching the 14.6-d period (ratio 2.87) and large out-of-transit swing, supporting folded stellar variability / V-shape binary over a quiet planet. Shape v_sigma -1.74 is flat but does not outweigh depth and secondary evidence.
